Of course. This is an excellent and realistic scenario. Here is a specific, actionable recommendation for the community health nonprofit.

### Executive Summary: The "Offline-First, Hub-and-Spoke" Approach

This approach prioritizes the most significant constraints: intermittent power, no field internet, and low digital literacy. It uses free, open-source software designed for humanitarian work and durable, cost-effective hardware.

*   **Field Staff (the "Spokes"):** Use rugged Android tablets with a simple data collection app that works entirely offline. They collect data throughout the day/week.
*   **Office (the "Hub"):** When staff return to the office (e.g., weekly or bi-weekly), they connect their tablets to the office Wi-Fi. The collected data automatically syncs to a central, cloud-based server. A designated data manager at the office can then view, clean, and analyze the information.

This model is resilient, simple for field staff, and requires zero recurring software costs, ensuring sustainability after the donor funding ends.

---

### Recommended Tools

1.  **Primary Software: KoboToolbox**
    *   **What it is:** A free and open-source suite of tools for field data collection, used extensively by NGOs, and humanitarian organizations (including the UN and Red Cross). It is perfect for this scenario.
    *   **How it works:**
        *   **Form Building:** An admin uses a simple web interface on a computer to create digital versions of your paper forms (e.g., patient intake, household survey). The interface is a drag-and-drop builder.
        *   **Data Collection (Offline):** Field staff use the **KoboCollect** app on an Android tablet. They download the blank forms once at the office. In the field, they can fill out hundreds of forms with no internet or power connection required.
        *   **Data Syncing:** Back at the office, they connect to Wi-Fi, open the app, and press "Send Finalized Form." All the data is securely uploaded to the KoboToolbox server.
    *   **Cost:** **Free.** KoboToolbox offers a free server for humanitarian organizations with unlimited forms and up to 10,000 submissions per month, which is more than enough for this team.

2.  **Hardware: Android Tablets & Power Banks**
    *   **Why tablets?** A larger screen is much easier for filling out forms than a phone, significantly reducing errors and frustration for staff with low digital literacy.
    *   **Recommended Model:** **Samsung Galaxy Tab A series** (e.g., Tab A8 or A9) or a similar reputable brand. They offer a good balance of durability, screen size, battery life, and cost. Avoid ultra-cheap, unknown brands which fail quickly.
    *   **Power:** High-capacity (20,000mAh) power banks for each field staff member. This will allow them to recharge their tablet 2-3 times, easily lasting a full week in the field without electricity.

3.  **Office Hub Hardware & Software**
    *   **Computer:** One reliable new laptop for the designated data manager/administrator.
    *   **Backup:** A Network Attached Storage (NAS) device (e.g., from Synology or QNAP). This is a small, dedicated box with hard drives that sits in the office. It will be used to automatically download and back up all data from the Kobo server daily, ensuring you have a local copy of your data that you own and control.
    *   **Analysis Software:** **LibreOffice** (a free alternative to Microsoft Office) or a discounted Microsoft 365 license for nonprofits. The data from Kobo can be easily downloaded as an Excel/spreadsheet file for basic analysis, charts, and reports.

---

### Budget Breakdown (Total: PHP 400,000)

This budget prioritizes durable hardware and essential training. All prices are estimates based on current market rates in the Philippines.

| Item | Description | Quantity | Unit Cost (PHP) | Total Cost (PHP) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Field Hardware** | | | | |
| Android Tablets | Samsung Galaxy Tab A9 or similar (8.7-inch) | 20 | 12,000 | 240,000 |
| Protective Cases | Rugged, shock-absorbent cases for tablets | 20 | 1,000 | 20,000 |
| Power Banks | 20,000mAh capacity from a reliable brand | 20 | 2,000 | 40,000 |
| **Office Hub Hardware** | | | | |
| Office Laptop | For data manager (e.g., Lenovo IdeaPad, Acer Aspire) | 1 | 40,000 | 40,000 |
| NAS Device | Synology DS223j or similar 2-bay NAS with 2x2TB drives | 1 | 18,000 | 18,000 |
| **Implementation & Training** | | | | |
| Training & Support | Hire a local IT consultant for 5 days of setup, form creation, and hands-on staff training. Includes creating simple, laminated user guides in the local language. | 1 | 25,000 | 25,000 |
| **Contingency Fund** | For unexpected costs, repairs, or replacements. | 1 | 17,000 | 17,000 |
| | | | **TOTAL** | **PHP 400,000** |

***Note on Staffing:*** This budget assumes ~20 of the 30 staff are field-based and require tablets. The remaining 10 are office/admin staff who can share existing or new office computers.

---

### Sustainability: What Happens After 18 Months?

This plan is designed specifically for long-term sustainability after the initial funding is gone.

1.  **Zero Recurring Software Costs:** The core of the system, **KoboToolbox and LibreOffice, is free.** There are no monthly or annual subscription fees to worry about. This is the most critical factor for sustainability.

2.  **Data Ownership and Access:** Your data is stored on the free Kobo server, but more importantly, it is automatically backed up to your own **local NAS device in the office**. Even if the Kobo service were to disappear, you would not lose a single piece of data. The office will still need an internet connection to perform the sync, but this is a standard operational cost the nonprofit likely already has.

3.  **Hardware Lifecycle:** The tablets and laptops are the only components with a limited lifespan (typically 3-5 years). The PHP 17,000 contingency fund can cover initial repairs. The nonprofit should begin planning immediately to set aside a small amount in its annual budget (e.g., PHP 50,000/year) for a gradual hardware replacement fund. This turns a future crisis into a predictable, manageable expense.

4.  **Human Capacity:** The initial training is not just about teaching staff to tap buttons. It's about **creating internal "Super Users."** By identifying 2-3 staff members who are slightly more tech-savvy, the consultant can give them extra training. These Super Users become the go-to internal support for troubleshooting and training new hires, eliminating the need to hire external help in the future. The system's simplicity ensures that this knowledge is easy to maintain and transfer.

By the time the 18-month funding period ends, the nonprofit will own all its hardware, have a robust and free system for data management, and possess the in-house skills to operate and maintain it for years to come.
